clue.text: Function room

definitions.meaning: a role or office, as in acting in an official ...
space available to hold things, as in a hall's seating limit

explanation.definitionFit: Both a role held and the amount of space available are standard senses of the same word.

clue.text: Kids stealing the gold, first one would question the official explanation

definitions.text: one would question the official explanation

parts.note: to kid is to trick or deceive, as cons do
piracy is theft, especially at sea
1ST, with the figure read as the letter I

explanation.surface: Children are caught pinching gold, and the first one doubts the official story.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who rejects official accounts in favour of a hidden plot is a believer in secret schemes.

clue.text: Animal with bite holding message up, demanding shellfish

indicators.note: in a down clue the whole assembled string is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: an elk is a large deer

indicators.note: the word for bite has the message placed inside it

parts.note: a wire is a telegram, an old message

explanation.surface: A snappy creature clutching a note insists on seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reverses the whole assembly, not just the message; 'demanding' only joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A periwinkle is a small edible sea snail, a kind of shellfish.

clue.text: Those with strain in voice, one being choked by endless work

indicators.note: the letter for one is squeezed inside the shortened word for work
the word for work loses its final letter

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone strained of voice is throttled by never-ending labour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts CHORE to CHOR, and I goes inside it. A strain is a tune, so singers carry a strain in voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A choir is a body of singers, people who carry a tune (a strain) with their voices.

clue.text: Mathematical study to fix on in book with essay

indicators.note: the words for fix and on go inside the word for book

parts.note: a tome is a large book
to rig is to fix dishonestly
an essay is an attempt, a try

explanation.surface: A maths subject is about rigging something in a book and writing an essay.
explanation.definitionFit: Trigonometry is the branch of mathematics dealing with triangles and angles.

clue.text: Telephone fuse?

definitions.meaning: playfully, a fuse is something that blows

explanation.definitionFit: The word is old British slang for a phone, and whimsically names anything that blows, as a fuse does.

clue.text: State positive European words maintained by Turner

indicators.note: the European yeses are held inside the actress's first name

parts.note: SI is Spanish or Italian for yes

explanation.surface: Turner backs some affirmative continental remarks.
explanation.walkthrough: One phrase supplies two pieces, the French and the Spanish or Italian word for yes; 'maintained by' sets them inside the actress's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Louisiana is one of the states of the USA.

clue.text: As I've said, surely there's no reason to suspend this type of lens

indicators.note: the phrase points to the spoken form of the words that follow

parts.words: surely there's no reason to suspend
parts.note: a rhetorical 'why dangle?', asking why anything should hang

explanation.surface: A speaker insists there is no point hanging up a certain lens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Why dangle' spoken aloud is heard as the lens name.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide-angle lens takes in a broader field of view than a standard one.

clue.text: Main chain putting price right up

indicators.note: in a down clue the pieces are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a fee is a charge or price

explanation.surface: A main chain is having its price pushed up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' is the sea, a crossword convention, so a main chain is a ridge in the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A reef is a ridge of rock or coral running near the surface of the sea.

clue.text: Bearing cold, accepting ordinary drug

parts.note: N, north, is a compass bearing

indicators.note: the word for cold takes the letter for ordinary inside it

explanation.surface: Someone carrying a chill takes an everyday medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: A narcotic is a drug that dulls the senses or induces sleep.

clue.text: Announced time for dessert

indicators.note: spoken out, so the word for a time is heard rather than seen

parts.note: a day of the week is a time

explanation.surface: A time was set for pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: A sundae is an ice-cream dessert with toppings.

clue.text: Tactical ploy where union has me put right with tuppence

indicators.note: corrected, so the letters are rearranged into proper order

explanation.surface: A trade union is fixed with a couple of pennies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put right' rearranges UNION, HAS, ME and PP together.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the art of gaining a tactical advantage over others, a stratagem for staying ahead.

clue.text: Where connections made, aces?

definitions.meaning: electrical sockets, where plugs are connected
playfully, cards that score strongly in bridge hand valuation

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means wall sockets, and whimsically the high-value scoring of aces at cards.

clue.text: Those touching appear good among more elegant clues

indicators.note: the letter for good goes inside the word for more elegant

explanation.surface: Touching ones show up as fine pieces of advice.
explanation.definitionFit: The ends of the fingers are the parts we touch things with.

clue.text: One used to find value in calculus objective written up in cast iron

definitions.text: One used to find value in calculus

indicators.note: the reversed objective goes inside the rearranged metal
cast metal is moulded into a new shape, so the letters are reshaped
in a down clue, writing upward reads the word backwards

parts.note: a target is an aim or objective

explanation.surface: A calculus tool has its aim engraved upward on cast iron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' rearranges the metal around the target, which 'written up' turns backwards because this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An integrator is a device or person that performs integration, finding values in calculus.

clue.text: Grazing land called pasture, ultimately

indicators.note: only the final letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: Grazing land is called pasture in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A range is a large open area of grazing land, especially in North America.

clue.text: Former work with Latin in old language

indicators.note: the reworked word and the letter for Latin go inside the language

parts.note: Erse is an old name for Scottish or Irish Gaelic

indicators.note: to work something is to shape it, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A former piece of work combines Latin with an old tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' looks like a noun meaning a job but is the anagram signal on 'with'; Erse is an old name for Gaelic.
explanation.definitionFit: Erstwhile is an adjective meaning former or onetime.

clue.text: Woman's release brings show of approval around middle of July

indicators.note: the word for applause goes round the central letters

parts.note: an ovation is a show of applause

indicators.note: only the central letters of the word are taken

explanation.surface: Applause greets something in mid-July.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of JULY is UL.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovulation is the release of an egg from a woman's ovary.

clue.text: Old sports venue uses broadcast in order to follow pass

indicators.note: the rest comes after the word for pass

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass

indicators.note: the rearranged word goes inside the order

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit

indicators.note: scattered widely, so the letters are scattered

explanation.surface: An ancient arena uses broadcasts in order to follow a pass.
explanation.walkthrough: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour; 'broadcast' scatters the letters of 'uses'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Colosseum in Rome was an ancient amphitheatre used for games.

clue.text: See 7
Bush's offensive, unsightly prospect receiving no backing — a mistake

indicators.note: the blemish takes the reversed word inside it

parts.note: a wart is an unsightly thing to behold

indicators.note: going backwards, so the word is reversed

explanation.surface: Bush's offensive is an ugly sight getting no support, and a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns the word 'no' round; Bush's campaign after 9/11 makes the whole answer apt.
explanation.definitionFit: The 'war on terror' was the military campaign launched by President George W Bush after 9/11.

clue.text: Slip away with greasy object to climb, heading for embarrassment

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing reads the word upwards, backwards

parts.note: a greasy pole, climbed at fairs

indicators.note: only the first letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: Someone escapes up a greased pole, red-faced.
explanation.definitionFit: To elope is to run away secretly to marry.

clue.text: Spooner's peaceful wind, which is agricultural

indicators.note: the initial sounds of the two words are swapped

explanation.surface: A gentle breeze of the agricultural kind.
explanation.walkthrough: The swap is by sound: in British speech 'calm' and 'farm' rhyme, so the L is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: A farm cart is an agricultural vehicle.

clue.text: See 22
Movement getting a soldier into trouble

indicators.note: the article and soldier go inside the word for trouble

explanation.surface: A soldier is getting into trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: A movement here is a section of a piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: An adagio is a slow movement in a musical work.

clue.text: See 1 down
Stuff the issue!

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both physical substance and the problem at hand.

clue.text: Chamberlain's vegetables captured by impressionist?

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', so the clue reads 'Chamberlain is ...' and the proper name stands for a person of that type, fair as the definition is by example

indicators.note: the vegetables are held inside the mimic

explanation.surface: Chamberlain's greens are seized by a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: Neville Chamberlain, British PM, appeased Hitler in 1938. 'Impressionist' suggests a painter but means mimic.
explanation.definitionFit: Neville Chamberlain is remembered for his policy of appeasement towards Hitler.
